title: Fast and Accurate Temporal Hypergraph Representation for Hyperedge Prediction

problem.claim: Temporal hypergraph representation learning must model high-order structure and temporal dynamics for temporal hyperedge prediction.

gap.claim: Multi-hop hyperedge-centric neighbor modeling has computational complexity that increases exponentially with model depth and quadratically with average hyperedge cardinality, limiting scalability.

contributions.claim: FastHeP is a temporal hyperedge prediction approach designed to handle large temporal hypergraphs.
An online hyperedge-centric neighbor store maintains time-aware and redundancy-aware node neighbors with stated theoretical guarantees.

A hybrid message-passing design models temporal high-order structures, combines local node-wise structure features with global hyperedge correlations, and provides a stated permutation-invariance guarantee.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the hybrid message-passing approach as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: FastHeP is reported to achieve up to two orders of magnitude speed-up against baselines.
FastHeP is reported to improve average accuracy by 5.1% against baselines.
The method is reported to have linear complexity with respect to model depth and average hyperedge cardinality.

narrative_sequence.summary: Temporal hypergraph representation learning combines high-order structure learning with temporal dynamics.
Existing multi-hop hyperedge-centric neighbor modeling is computationally expensive and limits scalability.
FastHeP addresses the scalability problem through an online neighbor store and hybrid message passing for temporal high-order structures.
Local graph-attention structure features are fused into global hyperedge correlations to produce temporal hyperedge embeddings.
Experiments report substantial speed-up and an average accuracy improvement over baselines.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links scalability to complexity growth with model depth and average hyperedge cardinality.

interpretation.claim: Controlling complexity along the dimensions that drive growth can support scalable high-order temporal modeling.

application.claim: For similar models, consider compact neighbor storage and complexity that is linear in model depth and average interaction size.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these complexity and performance properties hold beyond the reported experiments or task setting.

unknowns: Datasets, baseline identities, and experimental protocol are not specified.
The scope and assumptions of the theoretical guarantees are not specified.
The abstract does not provide absolute runtime or accuracy values.
